title: Kingfisher Private Access Topology Intake
summary: Intro discovery focused on how Kingfisher will connect Redwood private deployment into their AWS environment. Discussed VPC peering vs PrivateLink, transit gateway, egress IPs, region gating, and compliance needs. Agreed next steps: share network diagram template, SSO/SAML details, and propose pilot scope for a single region with dedicated NAT egress IPs.
action_items: Alicia Park; Send Kingfisher the private-deployment network diagram template + peering checklist; 2026-06-02
Marcus Reed; Prepare short runbook for NAT egress options and recommended IP allocation; 2026-06-04
Priya Nair; Share current AWS account IDs and preferred region for pilot; 2026-06-01
next_steps: Schedule follow-up technical deep dive with Kingfisher networking team (Marcus to lead)
Share Redwood Private onboarding doc + SOC2 and KMS slides
Define pilot region and provide preliminary cost estimate for Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-28 16:00 EDT — Duration ~47m
Attendees: Alicia Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Reed (Redwood SE), Jared Kim (Head of Platform - Kingfisher), Priya Nair (Cloud Architect - Kingfisher), Liam O'Connell (Security Lead - Kingfisher)
---
[00:00] Alicia: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, i'm Alicia, i'm the AE on this account. quick round robin?
[00:12] Jared: Jared here, quick hello, running platform at Kingfisher, we own infra for the ml services.
[00:18] Priya: Priya, cloud architect, i'll be the day-to-day contact for networking and region constraints.
[00:25] Liam: Liam, security and compliance, i'll flag anything with KMS, audit, or residency.
[00:32] Alicia: Great. Marcus from Redwood is our SE, he's going to walk through topology choices. Marcus?
[00:39] Marcus: Hey all, hi, thanks. goal today: understand your constraints for private access — do you want VPC peering, Transit GW, or AWS PrivateLink/private endpoints for Redwood? Also egress requirements and region gating.
[00:53] Jared: High level — we need private network-only access, no public egress for requests to models. We also need stable egress IPs for allowlisting to downstream partners and to our vendor S3 buckets.
[01:07] Priya: We're in three regions (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1) but pilot will be us-east-1. we might need us-east-2 later, region gating is important — we have data residency and latency rules per customer.
[01:25] Marcus: ok. two typical patterns: 1) VPC peering to a Redwood VPC (or we peer into your transit), 2) PrivateLink / Private Endpoints where we expose an ENI in your VPC and traffic stays private. each has tradeoffs.
[01:41] Priya: can you compare them on NAT/egress control? that's our main concern.
[01:47] Marcus: sure. with peering, traffic routing is straightforward but you manage egress. if you want a stable egress IP we recommend an egress NAT gateway in your control plane, or we can provide a dedicated NAT IP from Redwood if you take Dedicated with reserved egress — slightly messy wording there — basically dedicated egress IPs. with PrivateLink the endpoint lives in your VPC and egress is fully controlled by you, easier to allowlist.
[02:12] Liam: So PrivateLink looks nicer for allowlist, but what about performance and cost?
[02:18] Marcus: PrivateLink adds a per-GB data processing charge on top of inter-region data if you cross regions. peering is cheaper for inside-region traffic. Performance-wise latencies are comparable for same-region, PrivateLink may add a tiny hop. For high throughput, Dedicated pools in the same region reduce tail latency.
[02:37] Jared: We do plan for high throughput once we go live, primary use is embeddings ingestion and realtime chat features. Does Redwood support prefix/KV cache or whatever for reducing tokens?
[02:49] Marcus: Yes we have prefix and KV cache — sometimes transcribed as kv cash — sorry the speech-to-text bot mangled that — it caches model context to save tokens. That's more runtime, independent of network topology.
[03:03] Priya: ok. for peering: we use a Transit Gateway in our org, and we prefer to consolidate peering through TGW rather than many VPC peerings. can Redwood attach to our TGW?
[03:14] Marcus: Yes, we can connect via Transit Gateway attachments. Typical approach: Redwood creates a peer VPC in our account/partner account, attach to your TGW through a multi-account transit setup, or we accept peering to a Redwood-managed VPC that then routes to your TGW. We'll share a diagram.
[03:32] Alicia: note: for private deployments we have two flavors — Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) where you get dedicated GPU pools and options for fixed egress IP, and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) where control plane sits in your network. we'll clarify in docs.
[03:48] Liam: Security question — where are encryption keys stored? we need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs.
[03:55] Marcus: You can bring-your-own KMS in Private deployments; we integrate with customer KMS for model keys and audit trail. For Hosted, Redwood manages keys and we have SOC2, but for Private you can hold keys. We'll send SOC2 and KMS integration notes.
[04:12] Priya: For pilot: we want to validate egress IP stability (for allowlisting), latency SLOs under burst load, and an A/B test against our current vendor. what's the normal pilot scope?
[04:25] Alicia: Most pilots pick one region, small dedicated pool or Private deploying in a single VPC, 2-4 week perf run with our SE running benchmarks. Marcus will run a baseline with your sample workload.
[04:36] Marcus: Yep. We'll need sample payloads, expected QPS and burst characteristics, and whether you want streaming vs blocking APIs. Also need AWS account IDs and preferred subnets for PrivateLink endpoints or TGW attachments.
[04:52] Jared: QPS: baseline 150 req/s with bursts to 600 for 1-2 min, average token lengths moderate ~300 tokens. We'll share synthetic traces.
[05:02] Marcus: Great. On NAT/eIP: two options — you put a NAT gateway with Elastic IPs in your VPC and route traffic out (you control allowlist), or Redwood can provide egress IPs on Dedicated if you sign a reserved commit. If you need per-tenant IPs we can discuss a proxy layer but that's custom.
[05:22] Priya: What about cross-region? If RG wants eu users pinned in eu-west-1, can we keep data in region?
[05:29] Marcus: Yes, we can pin models and routing policies to region. For private deployments we deploy runtime in the region you specify. For hosted we have region options too but Private gives you full control.
[05:41] Liam: Audit logging — do we get token-level logs or just request metadata? Our compliance requires traceability but not storing raw prompts beyond retention policy.
[05:52] Marcus: We emit request metadata and optionally redacted request content for quality monitoring. For Private deployments you can configure retention and even ship logs to your SIEM. We'll include logging options in the onboarding doc.
[06:06] Jared: Ok can you summarize network artifacts you'll need from us?
[06:11] Marcus: AWS account IDs, VPC IDs and subnets for ENI endpoints, TGW IDs if using transit, routetable entries, list of allowed egress IPs (if you need allowlist), preferred regions, and whether you want us to provide a peer VPC.
[06:25] Priya: We prefer to avoid extra peer VPCs — TGW attach preferred. Also prefer PrivateLink for tenant isolation, but cost and throughput tradeoffs matter. Can you provide a cost delta?
[06:38] Alicia: We'll put together a brief cost comparison: PrivateLink pricing estimate, peering/TGW model, and Dedicated vs Private licensing delta.
[06:47] Jared: Any blockers on compliance? we need SOC2 and ISO 27001 docs and an option for customer-managed keys.
[06:55] Marcus: We have SOC2 Type II for hosted and full compliance package for Private with BYOK. I'll add links.
[07:02] Liam: also need SSO integration and RBAC — we run Okta.
[07:07] Marcus: Redwood supports SAML/Okta SSO and role-based access controls; we'll send examples of attributes.
[07:14] Priya: For networking specifics: subnets must be /20 or larger due to multiple ENIs? what's the subnet size requirement for PrivateLink endpoints?
[07:24] Marcus: We recommend /24 per endpoint at minimum, but if you plan many endpoints allow larger. We'll include a subnet sizing guide.
[07:34] Jared: Does Redwood require any ingress firewall rules on our side?
[07:39] Marcus: For PrivateLink you need to allow inbound from the endpoint network to the Redwood service port (TLS) — typically 443. For TGW or peering ensure routes to Redwood-managed CIDR are in route tables. We'll provide exact CIDR ranges.
[07:55] Alicia: quick cross-check: pilot timeline? are you targeting a production cutoff end of Q3?
[08:02] Jared: yes ideally pilot in June/July, production by late August.
[08:07] Alicia: ok. we'll aim to have diagrams and pilot proposal by next week.
[08:11] Priya: one more: what about egress to third-party APIs? we need to audit egress flows.
[08:17] Marcus: You can route egress through your NAT and apply inspection. For hosted/egress provided by Redwood that goes out under our IPs and we'd need contracts for allowlisting — not ideal for you. Private ensures all egress flows remain under your control.
[08:32] Jared: Good. let's talk about the security review — will you provide an artifact set we can hand to our legal/compliance team?
[08:39] Alicia: yes, we'll pack SOC2, encryption notes, ATE docs; i'll also add our standard DPA and suggested language for data residency.
[08:47] Liam: We may want a short technical deep dive on the TGW attachment and route propagation. can Marcus lead that?
[08:54] Marcus: yes, we'll schedule a 60m deep-dive with your network engineers.
[08:59] (brief audio interruption)
[09:10] Marcus: Sorry, back. quick note — if you want egress IP per region, we can provide guidance but Dedicated with reserved egress is the path we've used for stable IPs. For pure Private deployment inside your VPC you control egress entirely.
[09:28] Priya: Are there any infra limits we should watch for — ENI quotas or route table size?
[09:33] Marcus: Good call: ENI and security group rules are AWS limits. We'll include recommended quota requests. Also TGW attachments and route table entries can grow.
[09:44] Jared: can you share examples of customers with a similar setup?
[09:49] Alicia: we have a reference architecture doc and a 1-page case study for a fintech that used TGW+PrivateLink hybrid; we'll send links.
[09:59] Priya: Onboarding docs — we need a checklist we can give to networking to pre-provision subnets and roles.
[10:06] Marcus: We'll send a checklist that includes account IDs, VPC/subnet ranges, SG rules, preferred AZs, and pilot access keys.
[10:14] Jared: timeline: we will share creds and account info by 06/01. Pilot kickoff ideally 06/08 if you can provision quickly.
[10:22] Alicia: sounds good. Marcus, any specific questions for them offline?
[10:27] Marcus: just sample traces and expected encoded token sizes. Also do you require encryption in transit with specific ciphers?
[10:34] Liam: standard TLS1.2+ is fine, would prefer TLS1.3 where supported.
[10:39] Marcus: noted.
[10:42] Alicia: ok wrap up — we'll send: network diagram template, PrivateLink vs TGW cost delta, SOC2/KMS docs, and propose pilot scope.
[10:52] Jared: thanks. quick ask — can you also include an example routing table snippet?
[10:57] Marcus: yes, will include snippets and terraform examples.
[11:02] Priya: Great, thanks.
[11:05] Alicia: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invite for the technical deep dive.
---
End of transcript. (note: occasional transcription artifacts present; product names sometimes mis-cased e.g., 'Redwood Ded-icated' or 'kv cash')
